summary: Make omp-usage the sole quota producer: account displays, SLO budgets, pool scheduling and enforcement share configured usage.limits.observed windows; remove harness.limits and legacy AccountLimit weekly/five-hour fields.

replay.detail: The new replicated durable usage.limits.observed kind is retained independently of local writer configuration. Older members quarantine the unknown non-authority kind for replay after upgrade. Quota and credit evidence is projected per producer; configured writers are selected at read time. For each durable credit, terminal states are absorbing across hosts: redeemed wins over forfeited, and forfeited wins over available or unknown regardless of timestamp. Redeemed is positive evidence; forfeiture is inferred. Within a state class the newest measured_at wins, with claim ID breaking ties.

schema.detail: The rebuildable account-limit projection uses a fresh version 4 namespace and rebuilds from durable usage.limits.observed claims only. Historical harness.limits claims are not converted into provider evidence. A rebuildable latest-credit projection avoids replaying durable credit history on each SLO read.

rules.detail: retention.toml declares usage.limits.observed durable with no checkpoint pruning rule; producer evidence remains available for configuration changes and projection rebuilds. Rules version 27 and staging version 2 remove the obsolete harness.limits pruning rule; checkpoint participants need matching updated rule digests before sealing new checkpoints.

compatibility.detail: The [usage_limits] daemon configuration accepts a writers list. Empty or absent writers deny local producer appends and contribute no quota or credit evidence, while schema-valid replication remains accepted. The producer writes as its configured agent identity. AccountLimit now exposes windows with per-window percentages, measurement times, resets, coverage, source and host; legacy weekly/five-hour fields are removed without aliases. All quota consumers use this fold. Weekly enforcement requires reported, fresh evidence with a future reset. Harness context RateLimits and rate-limit liveness proof remain independent of quota accounting. During credit catch-up SLOs use no-data with progress in open current/explain strings; the closed client-v0 status enum is unchanged.

downtime.detail: No coordinated fleet restart or capability gate is required. Durable credit history has no finite retention bound, so first-open credit replay is deferred rather than blocking startup. Configured reads start resumable catch-up batches of at most 64 claim rows with a persisted cursor and release the writer lock between batches. Until complete, credit reads expose catching-up progress and SLOs cannot report success. Empty configuration with no projection skips initialization until a read or configuration change requires it.

manual.detail: Configure [usage_limits] writers with explicitly authorized omp-usage producer agent identities on every quota-consuming member, and restart after configuration changes. Upgrade checkpoint participants to matching rules before sealing new checkpoints. Upgrade usage clients together with the windows wire contract; old AccountLimit weekly/five-hour fields are no longer served.

recovery.detail: Before rolling back to an older binary with strict configuration parsers, remove the [usage_limits] section. Backup restore retains every schema-valid durable observation regardless of current writer configuration. After restore or an interrupted upgrade, derived credit catch-up resumes from its persisted cursor; quota and credit projections can be rebuilt from retained claims after upgrading again. Restored evidence remains excluded from observational folds until its writer is configured.
